name: AOS Conservation Grants
summary: Annual grants for non-commercial, hands-on projects that study, protect or restore orchids and their natural habitats anywhere in the world. International grants need an institution to administer the funds.
reporting: Multiyear projects report annually, and an article, webinar or video on the project goes to the AOS within six months of completion.

eligibility.rule: Non-US applicants have an institutional affiliation

status.quote: will be accepting applications for conservation grants until April 1, 2026.

geography.quote: All conservation-oriented projects, anywhere in the world, will be considered.

access.quote: The American Orchid Society grants awards for non-commercial conservation projects

window.quote: will be accepting applications for conservation grants until April 1, 2026.

reporting.quote: We require all multiyear projects to be reported on annually, and that an article, webinar or video featuring your project be submitted for publication by the AOS within six months of completion.

effort.quote: The Conservation Committee of the American Orchid Society (AOS) will be accepting applications for conservation grants until April 1, 2026.

eligibility.quote: An institutional affiliation is required for administration of international grants.

after_award.quote: We require all multiyear projects to be reported on annually

documents.quote: Please include in your resumé or CV a summary of previous work (generally 1 page will suffice).
Please include 1-3 letter(s) of recommendation from mentors, community partners, etc.
Project Budget must be submitted in US dollar amounts.
Foreign applicants are required to be associated with and provide a letter of support from an educational institution, government agency, NGO or similar not for profit organization.
Applications involving the removal of orchid plants, parts or seeds from the wild must include a letter of authorization from the appropriate governmental authority

documents: CV or résumé summarising previous work
Letter of support from an institution, for non-US applicants
Government authorization letter, if collecting orchids from the wild
